question.text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q3 FY2027 earnings release? (Gross margin (GAAP))
question.resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as the midpoint of the guidance range for Q4 FY2027 as stated in NVIDIA’s “Outlook” section of its Q3 FY2027 earnings press release, expected to be published on [NVIDIA’s investor relations site](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/) and the [SEC’s EDGAR system](https://www.sec.gov/) on November 17, 2026.

The unit value for revenues is billions of U.S. dollars, and it will be rounded to the nearest billion. GAAP gross margin will be rounded to the nearest tenth of a percent. GAAP operating expenses are in a unit value of billions of U.S. dollars and will be rounded to the nearest tenth of a billion dollars.
question.fine_print:
* If a single figure (not a range) is provided, that figure will be used.
* If multiple ranges or scenarios are presented, the primary range specified in the official “Outlook” or “Guidance” section will be used to resolve the subquestions.
* If NVIDIA does not issue guidance for Q4 FY2027 in the Q3 FY2027 release, the corresponding subquestion will be **annulled**.
* Only the originally published figure will be used; subsequent updates, corrections, or guidance revisions will be ignored.

research:
I could not find anything yet that settles this, but management has already pointed to the answer. On the August 26, 2026 call, CFO Colette Kress said gross margin should bottom in Q4 FY2027 at **71% to 72%**. Secondary sources agree on that range; I could not read the official transcript (the summary site is gated), so it is not verified word for word. If the actual guide lands inside that range, the midpoint of the question (68.95 to 73.05) is about 71.5%. GAAP guidance has sometimes come in 0.1 point below non-GAAP.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-08-26: The Q2 FY2027 release reports GAAP and non-GAAP gross margin of 75.0% on revenue of $96.2B. Its Q3 outlook is 74.0% ±50bp, the same for GAAP and non-GAAP, on revenue of $108.0B ±2%. It gives no explanation for the decline. [NVIDIA](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-second-quarter-fiscal-2027)
- The Q3 FY2027 release, which decides the question, has not been published. The question says it is due November 17; MarketBeat estimates November 18 after the close [MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-11-18-nvidia-co-stock/), and Kalshi's call-wording market also uses November 18.

## 2. Current status
- 2026-08-26: Several secondary sources report the 71% to 72% Q4 trough. They say margins would then settle at 72% to 73% in FY2028 once price increases already put through take effect, with memory costs as the main pressure. [TIKR](https://www.tikr.com/blog/nvidias-q2-earnings-beat-by-6-the-margin-guide-tells-a-different-story), [Platformaeronaut summary](https://transcripts.platformaeronaut.com/summaries/NVDA-2Q27-AI-Summary)
- 2026-08-26: Shacknews puts Kress's Q4 figure at "72%", a single number, and does not say whether it is GAAP or non-GAAP. [Shacknews](https://www.shacknews.com/article/150499/nvidia-nvda-gross-margin-decrease-fy27)
- Nothing settles the question yet. The verbal range points to roughly 71.5%, but the exact number is still open.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-27: The stock trades near $217. Management expects CPU revenue (Grace, and now Vera) to more than double in FY2028. [24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/27/nvidia-just-took-cpu-business-from-amd-and-intel-what-it-does-to-the-target/)
- 2026-10-26: Micron's revenue rose 379% to $54.2B, a sign of very strong memory pricing. That is the cost pressure on NVIDIA's margin. [time.news](https://time.news/nvidia-and-micron-drive-expected-sp-500-growth-data-shows/)
- 2026-09-03: Zacks repeats the 74% Q3 guide and the 71% to 72% Q4 trough. It quotes management saying "pricing conditions have become more difficult than previously expected." NVIDIA's supply and capacity commitments are $279B, mostly memory, and price increases start in FY2028. [Globe and Mail/Zacks](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/stocks/AMD/pressreleases/4424655/memory-costs-rise-can-nvidia-protect-its-70-gross-margin/)
- Another source says Kress tied the trough to "extreme memory pricing" caused by the AI buildout. [Implicator](https://www.implicator.ai/nvidia-70-percent-growth-forecast-margin-outlook.md)
- I found nothing from October 2026 in which management updated its margin commentary.

## 4. Base rates
- Recent GAAP gross margin guide midpoints:
  - Q2 FY2027: 74.9%, versus 75.0% non-GAAP; the actual was 75.0%.
  - Q3 FY2027: 74.0%, the same as non-GAAP. [Q1 FY27 release](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027)
- Actual GAAP gross margin:
  - Q2 FY2026: 72.4%
  - Q1 FY2027: 74.9%
  - Q2 FY2027: 75.0%
  - FY2026 full year: 71.1%, held down by a $4.5B H20 inventory charge. [10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000021/nvda-20260125.htm)
- GAAP guidance is usually equal to non-GAAP or 0.1 to 0.2 points below it.
- From memory, not re-checked: in FY2026, NVIDIA's earlier verbal margin targets ("mid-70s" by year end) were then reflected in the formal guides that followed.
- Change from the prior quarter's guide: this time the drop would be about 2 to 3 points (74.0% to about 71.5%), much larger than the usual move of 0 to 1.5 points.
- The ±50bp band has been the standard format in recent outlooks.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket, "NVDA Q3 adjusted gross margin (non-GAAP)": this is about the Q3 actual, not the Q4 guide, so it is only related. Prices: 73% to 75% at 0.845, 75% to 77% at 0.10, under 71% at 0.088. The market expects Q3 to come in near the 74% guide.
- Kalshi's markets on what NVIDIA will say on the November 18 call do not bear on the margin number.
- I found no market or published analyst consensus specifically on the Q4 FY2027 GAAP gross margin guide.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- NVIDIA usually announces its earnings date around late October; last year's notice came on 2025-10-29. [Barchart](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/35775850/nvidia-sets-conference-call-for-third-quarter-financial-results)
- Other companies' earnings could change the read on memory and pricing: Intel on October 29, plus Samsung and SK hynix commentary and memory contract prices.
- Possible charges that would push GAAP below non-GAAP, such as inventory or China-related items or acquisition costs; the Groq deal is under DOJ scrutiny, which Kalshi prices at 0.07 for a fine this year.
- The Q3 release itself (November 17 or 18): the Q3 actual compared with 74%, and whether the price increases are pulled forward or memory costs come in worse than expected.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 20 days remain. The Q3 FY2027 release is due November 17 or 18, 2026.

(b) The latest value from the resolution source is the Q3 FY2027 GAAP gross margin guide of 74.0% ±50bp, published August 26, 2026. The Q2 FY2027 actual was 75.0%. On the August 26 call, CFO Colette Kress said gross margin should bottom in Q4 FY2027 at 71% to 72%, according to secondary sources. I could not verify the transcript word for word.

(c) If nothing changes, the formal guide should reflect the stated trough. The likely midpoint is about 71.5%, or 71.4% if GAAP sits 0.1 point below non-GAAP.

(d) The current trend is memory cost pressure, "extreme memory pricing", with price increases only taking effect in FY2028. That supports a guide at the bottom-to-middle of 71% to 72%, so roughly 71.0% to 71.5%.

(e) Guide midpoints usually move 0 to 1.5 points from one quarter to the next. Here management has already signaled a drop of about 2.5 points. Formal guides have usually tracked earlier verbal targets within a few tenths of a point.

(f) There is no market or published analyst consensus on the Q4 guide. Management's verbal range points to about 71.5%. One source (Shacknews) quotes the Q4 figure as "72%". The Polymarket market on the Q3 actual expects about 74%, in line with the Q3 guide, so it adds no new information about Q4.

(g) Two scenarios could push the result outside the expected range:
- **Low:** Memory contract prices spike further, or there is a GAAP-only inventory, China or acquisition charge. Either could take the guide to about 70% or lower.
- **High:** Price increases are pulled forward, a better product mix arrives, or memory costs ease. Any of these could bring a guide of about 72.5% to 73%.

- NVIDIA has generally turned its verbal margin targets into matching formal guides.
- GAAP guidance is usually equal to non-GAAP or 0.1 to 0.2 points below it.

(f) **Experts and markets:**
- Secondary sources consistently report the 71% to 72% trough. Shacknews reports a single "72%".
- No market or published analyst consensus exists on the Q4 guide itself.
- Polymarket expects the Q3 non-GAAP actual to land between 73% and 75%, so it does not suggest an early collapse.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- *Low:* memory costs escalate further, or an inventory or China-related charge hits GAAP. The guide comes in at 70.0 to 70.5%.
